title: The Picture Of Dorian Gray with Joanna Lumley, Alfred Enoch, Stephen Fry & Fionn Whitehead - review
transcript: hello i'm paul seven lewis and welcome to one minute theater reviews and i'm reviewing the picture of dorian gray despite it being co-produced by five regional theaters with the involvement of many more it's not theater uh it's not filmed theater it's not a theatrical film it's not a theater film hybrid it's a film a bit of an avant-garde film maybe but a film so i can't call this a theater review but here's my film review the adaptation by henry phillo bennett of oscar wilde's novel brings us into the present day where dorian gray has been transformed into a social media star by a new filter that makes him incredibly attractive but he's corrupted by his obsession with his number of followers uh your followers meant more to me than i did his girlfriend says or as he says himself he chooses aesthetics over ethics and while the filter keeps his digital face in the bloom of youth his actual face starts to deteriorate rapidly recalling uh what they remember of him and of what happened to him are joanna lumley silky voiced as ever as an amoral lady in arbor and alfred enoch has a believably bad influence called harry both speaking to an interviewer played by stephen fry their performances are excellent as is russell tovia's basil uh the man who invents the filter although he appears less than the story would seem to demand well that's my one minute review keep watching to find out what i didn't like about the picture of dorian gray although a great deal of the film is in the form of people in isolation giving interviews or making calls or posting online it's not some fuzzy set of zoom calls it's beautifully filmed in proper settings and from varied angles there are cleverly cut sequences when flashbacks are required the main one conveying a party atmosphere surprisingly well in fact i found the filming and the cutting hypnotic thanks i assume to director tamara harvey so far so good but here's where my enjoyment started to buffer uh because pleasant looking and charming and demeanor as finn whitehead is and good actor as he undoubtedly is i just couldn't understand why the other characters fell in love with his dorian gray or why he would attract hundreds of thousands of followers i admit this may indicate my lack of understanding of the kind of people who do attract a massive following on instagram and the like of course i speak as someone who has hundreds rather than thousands of followers on social media and i did take to heart basil's declaration that youth is the one thing worth having i thought okay let's try a theatrical suspension of disbelief but the problem was i think that whether he was talking to his followers or his friends what came out of his mouth was vacuous and spoken in a flat voice it may have been meant to indicate the innocence of youth but to me it was just dull i could have written this off as my lack of appreciation of things youthful except that i did find emma mcdonald who played sybil another rising social media star entirely convincing in her voice and looks and that was as much to do with her expression as the basic tools she was working with as a warning against the dangers of social media henry philly bennett's script covers a well-clicked search and has little new to say the novelty of the way it says it soon wears off but i would say the acting and filming make it worth a view i give the picture of dorian gray three stars i hope you found this review useful as dorian says subscribe like comment or not which is probably why i'm not a social media superstar thank you for watching
